idiom_name: @Serializable WebLink data class + java.net.URI.resolve + ktor-client dereference
implementation_notes: Kotlin realizes the invariant with its existing JVM and Ktor primitives instead of a link-class hierarchy: the link is a @Serializable data class (kotlinx.serialization) carrying rel, href, method and type, so the value itself is the carrier across HTTP and process boundaries; the JVM's immutable java.net.URI supplies parse/resolve/normalize, letting a producer emit relative hrefs that the consumer resolves against a base URI at use time (late binding), and io.ktor.http.LinkHeader produces and parses RFC 8288 Web Linking Link headers when metadata rides in headers rather than the body. The classic producer/carrier/consumer class trio collapses into serializable data values plus URI.resolve plus a ktor-client request; a @JvmInline value class Rel keeps relation types from mixing with plain strings at zero allocation. Hand-written link registries and resolver classes remain justified for gateway-style hops that need rewriting, signing or redirect layers.
code_sketch:
@Serializable data class WebLink(val rel: String, val href: String,
                                val method: String = "GET")

val order = client.get(base.resolve("/orders/42")).body<Order>()
val pay = order.links.first { it.rel == "payment" }        // consumer follows, never rebuilds
val target = base.resolve(pay.href)                          // late binding via URI.resolve
val payment = client.get(target).body<Payment>()             // dereference the transferred link
pitfalls: Plain-String hrefs: most Kotlin HTTP/JSON stacks type links as String, so a raw href can be pasted into any URI-shaped slot; wrap links in a typed WebLink/Rel value or the compiler will not catch a swapped rel and href.

Relative hrefs sent straight to a client: ktor request() does not resolve against the previous response's URI - forgetting base.resolve(href) turns a valid HATEOAS link into a request-time failure only when the code path is exercised.

URI constructors throw URISyntaxException on malformed input and happily carry internal hostnames and ports; validate and absolutize link targets before handing them to untrusted consumers, and enforce authorization at resolution time rather than trusting the href.

io.ktor.http.LinkHeader documents itself as RFC 5988 while the current grammar is RFC 8288; hand-rolled parsers copied from the older grammar can mis-read newer link params (hreflang, title), and generic kotlinx.serialization silently drops unknown WebLink properties - model metadata explicitly.

Unbounded link chains: a follow-the-link loop inside coroutines without withTimeout or a visited set amplifies one dereference into runaway requests; @JvmInline Rel is also erased at runtime, so the relation-type safety is compile-time only.
